title: Publish an executable Git compatibility matrix
author: w0F5vYijNonu8kkqLSa_jYY4GIV-Q5HpbxYY525ggm4

events.title: Publish an executable Git compatibility matrix
events.body:
## Outcome

Publish one compatibility matrix generated by stock-Git probes through the real relay and desktop host path rather than by manually maintained claims.

## Implementation

- Extend the mesh end-to-end harness so a stock Git client performs full clone, fetch after branch and tag changes, owner push, delegated write push, rejected read-only push, rejected stale or tampered credentials, unprotected force-push, shallow clone, submodule checkout, and signed-commit preservation.
- After each accepted push, clone again and assert the pushed refs and object ids are served.
- Emit a stable `git-compatibility.json` report with `pass`, `fail`, or `unsupported`, the tested commit, and a concise reason for each probe.
- Render the same report in the capability documentation; do not maintain a second handwritten matrix.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every displayed capability is backed by an automated probe.
- A previously passing probe fails CI when it regresses.
- Unsupported operations are explicit and never presented as passing.
- Push tests prove authorized success, unauthorized rejection, and post-push cloneability.
- The harness runs without an external network.

## Dependencies

Depends on #434 so the harness runs in the standard workflow.

## Verification

Run the matrix generator twice against fresh temporary repositories and compare normalized operation ids, statuses, pushed object ids, and generated documentation data.

events.body:
## Outcome

Guarantee standard Git interoperability with a matrix generated entirely by executable probes through real repository-serving paths.

## Implementation

- Probe full clone, fetch, remote management, authenticated push, protected and unprotected force-push, branch and tag deletion, shallow clone, partial clone, submodules, bundles, signed commits, signed push certificates, local hooks, and unchanged third-party Git porcelain behavior.
- Delegate standard large-object probes to #467 and dependency-client probes to #455 while including their results in the same generated matrix.
- After each accepted write, clone again and assert exact refs and object identifiers.
- Emit a stable compatibility report with probe identifier, pass or fail, tested commit, route, and concise diagnostic.
- Render documentation only from the report and retain no handwritten capability claims.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every roadmap compatibility row is passing by the August 1 release gate; unsupported is allowed only as an in-sprint diagnostic and blocks release.
- Authorized writes, unauthorized rejection, protected-ref rejection, and post-write cloneability are proven.
- Partial, shallow, submodule, bundle, hook, signature, large-object, and dependency behavior each have an offline fixture.
- A previously passing probe regression fails continuous integration.
- No probe requires a live external service or personal credential.

## Dependencies

Depends on #434; consumes #441, #455, and #467 before release closure.

## Verification

Run the matrix twice against fresh repositories and standard client subprocesses, compare normalized reports and object ids, and inject one regression per operation family.
